HISD Ribbon

HISD's signature "Ribbon" graphic device — the canonical field expression. A solid brand-color field overlaid with a few soft, white, round-capped, low-opacity sweeping/looping strokes that sweep edge-to-edge across it like Houston's bayou currents. It is used full-bleed as a background behind content. The stroke composition comes from the shared line kit (ribbon-lines.js): pick a named lines preset or any integer seed — the same kit feeds both the static SVG shown here and the animated WebGL tier, so they always match. Every color derives from the --ribbon-* tokens (--ribbon-field-bg, --ribbon-stroke, --ribbon-stroke-opacity); the device is decorative (role="presentation" on the host, aria-hidden on the SVG) and all motion is paused under reduced-motion and forced-colors.

Variant gallery lines / seed

The same device, different deterministic compositions from the line kit. Each tile is a real generated composition: six named presets plus one raw seed. In code you choose them with the lines (preset name) or seed (integer) prop/attribute — the static SVG below and the animated WebGL tier are generated from the SAME kit call, so a given preset/seed always renders the same currents in both tiers.

Full-bleed hero field --animate

The device as a hero background: the .hisd-ribbon host paints the solid field via --ribbon-field-bg and inlines the white current strokes; sample content (wordmark + heading) sits on top. Any brand color may override the field per section. With --animate the two stroke sub-layers drift on slow, offset loops for a calm parallax current.

Both themes

The field-bg and stroke colors are theme-invariant, but --ribbon-stroke-opacity lifts from 0.16 (light) to 0.22 (dark) so the currents keep their presence on darker surroundings. Each panel sets data-theme; the static (un-animated) device is shown so the resting currents are visible. Both panels use the same lines="bayou" composition.

Fan divider --fan

A constrained-media accent (unchanged): a thin band of the fixed multi-stop --ribbon-fan brand sweep, for section rules in contexts where the full field device is too heavy. Shown static and animated.

Reduced motion & forced colors

The --animate drift is pure compositor motion: two stroke sub-layers (.hisd-ribbon__layer--a / --b) each run a long, offset @keyframes loop (~26s / ~39s) of a tiny translate + sub-degree rotate. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and under forced-colors: active the component ships an explicit animation: none !important block — zeroing a duration alone does NOT stop a running loop — so every current parks on its resting frame. In forced-colors the solid field flattens to the system canvas and the low-opacity white strokes vanish, so the field host gains a CanvasText border to keep its extent visible and the fan repaints as a solid CanvasText band. The frame below is the exact resting state a reduced-motion user sees (lines="crossing").

HISD

Static resting frame

Copy-paste snippet

<!-- Load tokens first, then the component styles -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="hisd-theme.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="ribbon.css">

<!-- Field device. Host = role="presentation"; inline SVG = role="img" aria-hidden.
     The host background IS the solid field (--ribbon-field-bg). The two stroke
     sub-layers carry .hisd-ribbon__layer--a / --b so CSS drifts each for parallax.
     The stroke paths are GENERATED by the shared line kit (ribbon-lines.js) — the
     markup below is the 'delta' preset; swap in any preset or seed composition.
     Override the field per section with any brand color via --ribbon-field-bg;
     raise --ribbon-stroke-opacity toward 0.22 on darker fields. Add --animate for
     the slow current drift. Place content in .hisd-ribbon__content to layer it
     on top. With the React (<Ribbon lines="delta"/>) or Web Component
     (<hisd-ribbon lines="delta">) adapter this markup is produced for you. -->
<div class="hisd-ribbon hisd-ribbon--animate" role="presentation"
     style="--ribbon-field-bg: var(--hisd-purple-500); --ribbon-stroke-opacity: 0.22;">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice" role="img" aria-hidden="true">
    <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="var(--ribbon-field-bg, #00A3AF)"/>
    <g fill="none" stroke="var(--ribbon-stroke, #ffffff)" stroke-linecap="round" opacity="var(--ribbon-stroke-opacity, 0.16)">
      <g class="hisd-ribbon__layer hisd-ribbon__layer--a">
        <path d="M-90,117.7 C57.4,200.9 20.2,286.6 -90,369.9" stroke-width="186" opacity="1.00"/>
        <path d="M139.8,1170 C320.9,784.6 172.3,465.6 -90,183.4" stroke-width="126" opacity="0.85"/>
      </g>
      <g class="hisd-ribbon__layer hisd-ribbon__layer--b">
        <path d="M932.4,1170 C216.6,750.8 1546.6,328.7 938.4,-90" stroke-width="179" opacity="0.95"/>
      </g>
    </g>
  </svg>
  <div class="hisd-ribbon__content"> … your wordmark + heading … </div>
</div>

<!-- Fan divider: a thin tokenized band (constrained-media accent). No inline SVG
     needed; --animate adds a slow horizontal sweep. Size with --hisd-ribbon-fan-h. -->
<span class="hisd-ribbon hisd-ribbon--fan" role="presentation"></span>

<!-- Sizing: the host fills its container's width; give the host (or a wrapper)
     a height via --hisd-ribbon-h or a block-size on the wrapper. -->
<div class="hisd-ribbon" role="presentation" style="--hisd-ribbon-h: 16rem;"> … </div>
